newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves aluminium company expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: India approves aluminium company expansion plans.

text.p: The Indian government has approved a mines ministry proposal to expand state-run National Aluminium Company Ltd's (NALCO) bauxite mines and alumina refinery, a ministry statement said on Wednesday.

The statement said the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved expansion of NALCO's bauxite mines to 4.8 million tonnes per year from 2.4 million and alumina refinery to 1.575 million tonnes from 0.8 million.
The expansion of the bauxite mines and alumina refinery will involve an investment of 16.65 billion rupees and will be implemented in 51 months, the statement said.
The project is expected to provide direct employment to an additional 881 people, it said.
NALCO has a market share of 35 percent in the domestic aluminium sector and has state-of-the-art technology for alumina and aluminium production.
"The expansion project is to be funded through internal resource generation, suppliers credit and loans but without any budgetary support from the government," the statement said.
It said the company was expected to earn an additional 5.4 billion rupees from alumina exports after the completion of the expansion programme.
